justification: Changes where every DCP extraction starts a section. A wrong rule either keeps filing real rules under false keys or merges a real section into its neighbour.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_dcp_section_headings.py tests/test_dcp_extraction_fidelity.py tests/test_dcp_review_enqueue.py -o addopts= -q
falsifiable_check.fails_when: A line whose heading code is a bare year or R plus one digit starts a section, a lone number above a zone-code table row starts a section, or a real heading ('B3 General Development Controls', 'E1 Caddens', '4.2 R2 Low Density Residential', '6 R3 Medium Density Residential zone controls', 'R10 Road reserves') stops matching.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: 68 passed. Mutations: junk-code filter off -> 4 failed; every letter+number code treated as junk -> 1 failed; table-row rule off -> 1 failed; line-break condition ignored -> 1 failed (after adding the one-line '6 R3 ...' fixture; it survived without it). Real PDFs, old vs new extractor: georges_river part 3 drops keys '2021' and 'R2', gains the real 3.16.2, and 3.13 (Parking, Access and Transport) regains 6,852 words that sat under '2021'; penrith D2 drops 'R1','R2','R3' and gains the real 2.1.3, 2.1.5, 2.3.2, 2.3.3; city_of_sydney section 3 drops '2012' and 'R1' and gains the real 3.16.5; total words within 0.1% in each.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: Production regulatory_provisions 2026-09-17: 11 live provisions keyed by a year or R-digit heading across 6 councils (7 served), e.g. city_of_sydney __R1 signage controls, georges_river __R2 access-handle table, parramatta __R2/__R3 height limits; and the current-hash auto-rejections of such rows that block city_of_sydney section 3 and georges_river part 3.

pre_impl.existing_data: 11 live junk-keyed provisions (canterbury_bankstown 2, city_of_sydney 2, georges_river 1, parramatta 4, penrith 2); rejected junk_ref queue rows at the current hash block city_of_sydney section 3 (2) and georges_river part 3 (1).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: junk_ref was treated as a garbage row to auto-reject; the rows are real rules under a false heading, so rejecting them blocked the chapter and making the rejection non-blocking would have left live rules on old text.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reuses the _JUNK_REF shapes (bare year, R plus a digit) at heading detection; enqueue_review_changes already supersedes prior rejections on a fresh --review, so no queue change is needed.

functions.name: is_junk_heading
functions.input: A SECTION_RE match's code, title and matched text.
functions.output: True for a bare-year or R-digit code, or a bare number whose title on the next line opens with a zone code; False otherwise.
functions.if_none: An empty code or title is not junk unless the code itself matches.

functions.name: _find_heading
functions.input: A council's section pattern and one page (or segment) of extracted text.
functions.output: The first heading match on the page that is not junk; a prefix-word heading still wins.
functions.if_none: None when every match on the page is junk, so the text stays in the section already open.

values.if_missing: Table rows and figure labels start sections again and their rules are auto-rejected under junk keys.

break_it.scenario: A DCP structured by zone has a real heading '4.2 R2 Low Density Residential' or '6 R3 Medium Density Residential zone controls'.
break_it.what_happens: Skipping it would merge the zone's controls into the previous section.
break_it.how: Only a bare R-digit code or a lone number above a zone-code line is skipped; a one-line heading that names a zone keeps matching. Pinned by test_zone_named_headings_on_one_line_still_match.

break_it.scenario: A council uses letter+number chapter codes (woollahra B3, penrith E1, C2).
break_it.what_happens: Treating every letter+number code as junk would lose whole chapters' headings.
break_it.how: Only R followed by a single digit is junk. Widening to [A-Z]\d+ failed test_real_letter_and_number_codes_still_match.

break_it.scenario: Skipping a junk heading makes the next table row on the page the heading (georges_river p43 read '6' / 'R3 Medium Density Residential' as section 6).
break_it.what_happens: A junk key the review gate does not recognise would be committed silently.
break_it.how: A bare number whose title starts on the next line with a zone code is also skipped; the page resolves to its real heading 3.16.2. Pinned by test_a_table_cell_number_above_a_zone_row_is_not_a_heading.

break_it.scenario: Live junk-keyed rules on chapters that are not re-read.
break_it.what_happens: They stay live under their junk keys until the chapter is re-extracted.
break_it.how: The fix applies at extraction; city_of_sydney section 3 and georges_river part 3 need a --review re-read after deploy, and parramatta, penrith and canterbury_bankstown chapters change on their next re-read. Recorded as residual risk.
break_it.repro: SELECT source_council, ref_number FROM regulatory_provisions WHERE is_current AND ref_number ~ '__((19|20)[0-9]{2}|R[0-9])$'

mutation_analysis: Junk-code filter off -> 4 failed; letter+number all junk -> 1 failed; table-row rule off -> 1 failed; line-break condition ignored -> 1 failed. Unmutated 68 passed.
residual_risk: Existing junk-keyed live rules change only when their chapter is re-read. Other table-row shapes that read as headings (a number above a non-zone title) are not addressed.

post_merge.manual_verify: After deploy, python scripts/dcp_extract_changed.py --review --council georges_river --chapter part-3-general-planning-considerations (and city_of_sydney section-3-general-provisions): no queued ref ends in a year or R-digit, and no current-hash rejected row remains for the chapter.
